_note: MyThuso for Mom: the plan a son or daughter pays for a parent. The three tiers, their prices and what each names are the Master Blueprint v4, Part D, which the founder confirmed on 14 September 2026 replaces the single R249 Thuso Mom this preview carried. The web reads this file; scripts/emit-plans.mjs writes it into Swift and Kotlin. No price here is typed anywhere else, and business-model.json's `mom` subscription points at this file rather than holding a number of its own.
_settingsNote: Since 15 September 2026, when the founder instructed that open questions become admin settings, the plan's name and each tier's name, whether a tier brings the tier below it, how many urgent call-outs Plus brings and over what period, what priority SOS means and whether WhatsApp is used after a visit are Money's settings in packages/catalog/money.json. This file holds the words each is read into and never a value: a key ending From names the setting, and packages/engines/src/money/domain/settings.ts reads the value in force into these words. The two open questions this file carried and the undecided priority SOS are those settings now, each with a proposal an admin may change.
_honestyNote: Every inclusion names the capability in packages/catalog/capabilities.json that it depends on, and every screen renders that capability's notice beside it. Nothing a tier names is real today, and the valuable half of this file is the refusals: the sentences that stop a plan price from being read as a device that exists, a place ahead of somebody more unwell, or medical-aid cover.

payer.headline: A nurse for your parent, paid for by you.
payer.statement: The person who pays is usually not the patient. It is the son or daughter in the city, looking after a parent who cannot easily get to a clinic, with the same nurse every time and a report after every visit.

tiers.why: Phase 2 because the Blueprint's roadmap ships Mom Essential in months 6 to 9, beside Chronic Routine and CCMDD collection, which this catalogue already places in phase 2.

includes.text: A nurse visit every month: blood pressure, glucose, weight, a medicine check and how they are doing
Chronic medicine collected from the CCMDD pick-up point or the clinic, with their authorisation, and delivered

values.off: A report and a photo after every visit, in the app
values.notify-only: A report and a photo after every visit, in the app, and a WhatsApp message saying it is ready

tiers.why: Phase 3 because the Blueprint's roadmap ships Mom Plus and Premium in months 10 to 12, with MamaThuso and the first carers.

includes.text: A registered doctor reviews every visit
A Thuso Band with an SOS button

tiers.why: Phase 3, for the same reason as Plus.

includes.text: A Thuso Home station, for video calls with the doctor and the family
Carer hours for bathing and meals

stacking.why: Said once above a tier's own items, naming the tier below, rather than repeating that tier's items: the repeated lines would each need their notice again, which is the stacked-notice defect the capabilities contract was written to end. With the setting off, the line is not drawn and each tier lists only what it names.

callOuts.none: With nought call-outs set, Plus lists no call-out line rather than one that promises nothing.
callOuts.why: The words the number and the period are read into, so "One urgent nurse call-out a month" is worked out from the setting and never typed. counts holds a word for every number the setting's bounds allow above nought, and the build fails when it does not.

addOns.statement: These have been named and not priced, so none of them shows a price and none can be added.

items.name: A second parent, at a discount

splitting.statement: Brothers and sisters would split the bill between them in the app. No share has been set, and nothing is split today.

refusals.sentence: No plan counts a device as included while the device does not exist. Thuso Band and Thuso Home have not been built, and every plan that names one says so beside it.
No plan buys a place ahead of somebody else. When two people need a nurse urgently, the one who is more unwell is seen first, whatever either of them pays.
MyThuso for Mom is not medical aid, and no medical scheme pays for it. It pays for no hospital care, test or medicine beyond collecting what has already been prescribed.
Paying for your parent's plan does not let you see their health record. The report and the photo after a visit reach you only if your parent has agreed, and they can stop them.

economics.why: The Blueprint's Part E: MyThuso for Mom retains R80 to R400 per parent per month. It is an indicative figure from the plan, not a trading result. No visit cost or nurse share is derived from the tier prices, because the documents give none per tier, and packages/catalog/earnings.json pays a visit inside a plan at the same rate as the same visit booked on its own.
